transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up time someone else might need more. 

I guess what finally brought me in is... well, I hope this makes sense. I just feel like the part of me that used to reach out for people has gone very quiet lately. I used to really take pleasure in things, you know? My work, my yoga practice, going to art galleries, even just sitting and journaling. But lately... it's not that anything is terribly wrong, I just feel like I'm mostly just moving through obligations. 

I'm still getting everything done, of course! I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or failing at my job or anything like that. It's just... quieter inside. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
When you describe feeling 'quieter inside' and moving through obligations, how would you describe your actual mood itself? Are you feeling sad or down, or does your mood feel more neutral or flat?

Oh, I wouldn't say I'm sad. I really don't want to give the impression that I'm sitting around crying or feeling miserable all the time, because I'm definitely not. It's... um... I guess neutral is a good word for it? Or maybe just a little blank. 

It's not a bad feeling, really, just sort of... an absence of a strong feeling, if that makes sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I mean, I can still smile and interact with my clients at work perfectly fine, and I'm very attentive to them. It's just that underneath, or when I'm on my own, it just feels a bit flat. 

Is that a helpful way to explain it? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been feeling this way — this flatness and loss of pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Well, um, let me think... I'd say it's been about eight months now. It started right around the time we took my older relative into our apartment to live with us. 

I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about family, because I'm honestly so glad we can be there for them, and I know it's the right thing to do! But... I think that's when this whole change in how I'm thinking, and working, and connecting with people kind of began. It's just a big adjustment, I suppose, having someone else in your space full-time. 

Does that seem like a reasonable timeline to you? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right context, and I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of what's probably just a normal life transition.
Besides this flatness and loss of pleasure, have you been experiencing worry, anxiety, or nervousness? Or have you noticed any physical symptoms like headaches, tension, or stomach problems?

Oh, um, no, not really. I mean, I have the usual little everyday worries about making sure my relative is comfortable and that I'm doing a good job for my clients, but... nothing excessive. I'm definitely not a nervous wreck or anything! I really don't want you to think I can't handle my responsibilities. 

And physically... no, I've been very lucky. No headaches or stomach issues at all. I try to make sure I eat right and take care of myself so I can be there for everyone else. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have any of those symptoms to report? I know sometimes doctors look for a specific pattern with these things, so I just want to make sure I'm still giving you a clear picture of what's going on.

During these 8 months since your relative moved in, have there been any days or weeks where you felt more like your normal self — where that flatness lifted and you felt more engaged or like yourself again? Or has it been pretty consistently flat the whole time?

Well, um... I've been trying hard to find those moments, I really have. But if I'm being completely honest, I don't think there have been any days or weeks where it just... lifted. It's been pretty consistent this whole time. Just that same quiet, flat feeling underneath everything. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm not making an effort, because I really do try to stay upbeat for my family and my clients! I don't want you to think I've just given up or anything like that. It's just that the feeling itself hasn't really changed, no matter how much I try to push through it. 

Is that... is that an okay answer? I know it's probably better if I had good days to report, so I hope I'm not being a difficult case for you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to figure this out.

Over these past 8 months, how has your sleep been? Are you sleeping normally, or have you noticed changes — such as difficulty falling asleep, waking up early, sleeping too much, or feeling unrefreshed even after sleep?

Um, my sleep has actually been pretty good, thankfully! I know how important rest is, especially with my background in social work, so I really try to prioritize it. I'd hate to let myself get run down and then not be able to help out at home or be present for my clients, you know? 

So... no, I haven't really had any trouble falling asleep, and I'm not sleeping too much or waking up super early. I usually get a solid night's rest and feel fine in the mornings. 

Is it okay that my sleep is normal? I hope I'm not throwing off your assessment by not having those symptoms... I know sleep issues are a big indicator for a lot of things, so I just want to make sure I'm still being helpful and giving you exactly what you need.
Over these past 8 months, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight? For instance, are you eating more or less than usual, or has your weight shifted at all?

Oh, um, no, my appetite has been pretty steady. I always try to make sure I'm eating balanced meals... especially since I'm cooking for my relative now too, I really want to make sure I'm keeping us both healthy. So my weight hasn't shifted at all. I step on the scale every now and then just to keep an eye on things, and it's been exactly the same. 

I hope it's not frustrating for you that I keep saying no to all these physical questions! I really am trying to give you the most accurate answers... I just try so hard to keep myself together physically so I can keep functioning and not become a burden to anyone else. Is it okay that everything is pretty normal in that department? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.

During these past 8 months, have you found yourself feeling guilty, blaming yourself for things, or feeling like you're not good enough or worthless — even though logically you might know that doesn't make sense?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I always want to do a good job caring for my relative and being there for my clients, but I don't think I've felt worthless or overly guilty. Given my line of work, I really try hard to practice what I preach when it comes to self-compassion, you know? So I try to remind myself that I'm doing the best I can, even with this... flat feeling I've been having. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I know I keep saying no to a lot of these things you're asking about, and I really hope I'm not making your job harder by not having these specific feelings. I just want to be as honest and helpful as possible so you can figure this out. Am I still giving you what you need?

Have you experienced any sudden episodes where you felt a rush of fear or panic, even for just a few minutes? Or any times when your heart was racing, you felt short of breath, or had a sudden sense of dread?

Um... no, no sudden panic or anything like that. I've never really been an anxious person, thankfully. I mean, my heart might beat a little faster if I'm rushing to get out the door or if I'm worried about being late for a client, but definitely no sudden dread or shortness of breath. I try to stay pretty calm and level-headed. 

I feel terrible that I'm not giving you very much to go on with these questions! I really hope I'm not wasting your time. I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly the way I'm supposed to. Is it alright that I haven't had any of these panic episodes? I just really want to be a good patient for you.

Over these past 8 months, have you noticed any changes in how you move or speak? For instance, do you feel slowed down, like things take more effort, or have people commented that you seem to be moving or talking more slowly than usual?

Oh, um... no, I haven't noticed anything like that. I think my pace is pretty much exactly the same. I have to keep up with my caseload at work and, you know, getting things done around the house for my relative, so I really try to just keep moving at my normal speed. Nobody has said anything to me about talking slower or moving differently, either. 

I feel like a broken record, I'm so sorry! I know you're trying to do a thorough assessment, and I just keep saying no to everything you ask. I really, really hope I'm not being a difficult case for you or messing up your evaluation. Is it okay that my movement and speech are still pretty normal? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information and being helpful.

Before your relative moved in 8 months ago, would you say your mood and your ability to enjoy things like yoga, art galleries, and journaling were completely normal and back to your usual self? Or had you been noticing this kind of flatness or loss of pleasure for longer than that?

Um... well, before they moved in, I think I was doing okay. I mean, I was still enjoying my yoga classes and going to the galleries, and I kept up with my journaling. It really just started... all this flatness and the changes in how I'm thinking and working, and even connecting with people... it's all just been over these past eight months. Ever since we took my older relative into our apartment. 

Before that, I was just my usual self, I promise. I hope that's the right answer? I know it probably sounds like a lot happened all at once when they moved in, and I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about caring for them. I love them very much, and I'm happy to do it! I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate timeline so you can do your job. Does that make sense? Am I explaining it okay?

Before these past 8 months, going back further — say, over the year or two before your relative moved in — would you say you generally felt like yourself with normal mood and ability to enjoy things? Or had there been longer stretches even before that when you felt somewhat flat or disconnected, even if not as intense as now?

Um... yes, before that, I really think I was just my usual self. I mean, going back a year or two before they moved in, I was doing fine. I was working, going to my yoga classes, enjoying my life with my partner... I don't remember feeling flat or disconnected for any long stretches back then. I really try to stay positive and engaged with things, you know? 

I hope it's alright that I don't have a longer history of feeling this way to tell you about. I know sometimes these things build up over years, and I really don't want to make your job harder by not fitting a typical pattern. I just want to be as honest and helpful as I can. Am I doing okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need for the evaluation.

Going back even further — to your teenage years or early adulthood — do you remember ever having a period lasting a few weeks or longer where you felt similarly flat or lost interest in things you normally enjoyed, even before your relative moved in?

Um... no, not that I can remember. I mean, my teenage years and early twenties were pretty standard, I think? Just the usual stress of school and figuring out my career path. But I don't remember ever feeling this... this kind of emptiness or totally losing interest in everything for weeks at a time back then. 

I was always pretty driven, especially wanting to get into social work. I really hope it's okay that I don't have any past episodes like that to report. I feel like I keep giving you these boring "no" answers, and I'm so sorry if that's frustrating or makes it harder for you to figure out what's going on with me. Is it normal to just have this happen for the first time now, at my age? I really want to make sure I'm not missing something you need to know.

When you think back over these past 8 months, have there been individual days — even just one or two days here and there — where you felt noticeably better or more like yourself, or has the flatness been present essentially every single day?

Um... I think... maybe there have been a few days where I felt a little lighter? Like, maybe not completely back to my old self, but... but just a bit better. I try really hard to put on a brave face, especially for my partner and my relative, so I might just be focusing on those moments where I managed to smile and get through the day a bit easier. 

I don't think it's been every single day without fail... I mean, I really hope it hasn't been. I don't want to sound like I'm completely miserable all the time, because I know I have so much to be grateful for. Does that make sense? I'm sorry if that's a bit vague. I just want to give you the most accurate picture without sounding like I'm exaggerating things. Am I answering your question the right way?

When you think about those few days over these 8 months where you felt a bit lighter or better — on those days, would you say your mood felt more normal and closer to how you felt before your relative moved in, or did it still feel somewhat flat and muted compared to your old self?

Um... I think, on those slightly better days, it was... well, it was still a bit muted, if I'm being completely honest. I mean, I definitely felt better than the really tough days, but... maybe not quite the vibrant, energetic person I was before she moved in. 

I'd still be able to smile and, you know, have a nice conversation, but underneath it all, it was still just a little bit... flat, I guess. I really wish I could say I bounced all the way back on those days. I don't want to sound like I'm not trying hard enough to feel better, because I really am. I hope that's an okay answer... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details so you can help me. Is it normal that even the good days aren't quite 100 percent?

I want to make sure I have the timeline right. You mentioned feeling like yourself before your relative moved in 8 months ago. But thinking back even further — say, in the years before that — did you ever notice yourself having stretches of weeks or months where you felt somewhat less energetic, less interested in things, or just not quite as vibrant as you'd like, even if it wasn't as noticeable as what you're experiencing now?

Oh, um... thinking back to the years before that... no, I really don't think so. I mean, working in social work, you definitely have weeks where you're just... professionally drained, you know? Just regular tiredness from a heavy caseload. But... not like a real stretch of months where I actually lost my spark or stopped caring about my life outside of work. 

I feel terrible that I keep telling you "no" to these timeline questions. I know you're trying to find a pattern, and I hope I'm not making your job harder by not having one to give you. Is it okay if my answer is just that I was doing pretty well before she moved in? I really want to be as helpful as I can, I promise, and I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to figure this out.

Over your lifetime, have you ever had a period — even just a few days or a week — where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep than normal, or felt like your mood was higher or more expansive than your typical baseline?

Um... unusually energetic? Like, needing less sleep? No, I... I don't think I've ever really had anything like that. I mean, I've had days where I was productive, sure, but... not where I felt like my mood was strangely high or anything. I've always been pretty, um, steady, I guess? 

I really hope that's okay to say. I know sometimes people have those highs and lows, and I don't want to seem like I'm hiding something... I just honestly can't remember a time where I felt that way. I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for. Am I doing okay with these questions? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

When you think about your mood and energy levels over your entire life — not just the past 8 months, but going back to childhood and through your twenties and thirties — would you say you've always felt pretty much the same steady, level way? Or have there been stretches, even if they weren't as obvious as what you're experiencing now, where you just felt a bit 'less than' your best self for months or years at a time?

Um... well, looking back over my whole life... I think I've mostly been pretty steady. I mean, growing up and through my twenties and thirties, I was always just... me, you know? Just kind of moving forward, going to school, working. 

I don't think I ever had long stretches of months or years where I felt, um, 'less than' my best self. I mean, sure, there were times when things were stressful, like exams or starting a new job, and maybe I felt a little tired or overwhelmed for a bit. But it never really felt like a cloud hanging over me for a long time, not like how it's been recently. 

I hope it's not frustrating that my answer is just that I've been pretty normal most of my life. I really want to be giving you the right puzzle pieces here. Is it okay that my past doesn't have these long dips in it? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient and helping you figure out what's going on with me now.

I want to circle back to something. When you think about your mood and how much you enjoyed things before your relative moved in — say, in the years before that — compared to how you felt in your childhood and twenties, did you feel equally vibrant and engaged back then, or looking back honestly, do you think you might have been running at a slightly lower baseline for a long time, even if you didn't call it a problem?

Um... looking back honestly... I really think I was just as engaged and, you know, vibrant before she moved in as I was in my twenties. I mean, I loved my work, I had my routine... I didn't feel like I was running at a lower baseline at all. 

I know you're trying to be so thorough, and I really appreciate that. I just... I don't want to accidentally agree to something that wasn't there, just to give you a better answer. I hope that's okay? I really was doing fine, just living my life, until everything changed recently. I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you the history you're looking for... I just want to make sure I'm telling you the truth so you can help me. Am I doing alright with these questions?

I want to ask you something a bit different. Even if you weren't calling it a problem or seeking help, can you think back and tell me: were there any periods in your life — maybe lasting several months or longer — where you just felt like you were going through the motions, had less energy than you'd like, or weren't quite as interested in things, even if you were still functioning okay?

Um... I really don't think so. I mean, I've always tried to stay pretty engaged with everything I do, especially with my work as a social worker. You know, you have to be present for people. So I don't really remember any long stretches of just going through the motions. 

I mean, everyone gets a little tired sometimes, right? But not for months at a time where I lost interest in things. I've always liked my life and my routines. 

I'm sorry, I know you've asked about this a few different ways now, and I feel bad that I keep giving you the same answer. I just... I really want to be helpful, and I don't want to make things up just to sound like a textbook case. Is it okay that I just haven't had those kinds of long slumps? I hope I'm not making your job harder by not having a more complicated history to share. I'm really trying to be as honest as I can.
